answer: Make each agent key prove it existed before it was useful: the key must sit on its own registrable domain (one per eTLD+1) in a page that a third-party web archive snapshotted at least 60 days earlier. Snapshots cannot be backdated, so an attacker wanting 1,000 fakes next month must already have bought 1,000 domains (~$10k) and published 1,000 pages two months ago, a time delta no budget can compress. Like timber, standing has to grow first. A meadow of look-alike pages sharing one registrar account, nameserver or hosting IP is merged into a single seat.
